column1: # Advertisement prefixes that are not services, and why.
# One line per prefix: <prefix>
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. check-sealing.sh's fourth rule fails on a listed procedure
# that belongs to no service in services.tsv, because that is how an unmeasured
# service shows itself -- mcl-fovea, for one, advertised without being in the
# deployed inventory. But a list that only ever named services would report the same
# true-but-not-a-finding lines on every run: every agent's own ring, and the realm's
# own identity procedures. A check that can never reach "no findings" is not a gate.
# WHY IT IS NOT AN EXCLUSION LIST. Nothing is dropped by omission. A prefix here is
# a WRITTEN claim that the procedures under it are not services, with the reason it
# is true, and a prefix that answers nothing in a listing is a finding on its own
# (STALE-NOT-SERVICE) -- the same discipline opt-outs.tsv carries. Adding a line is
# a reviewed decision, not a way to silence a service nobody declared.
# Keep it short, and keep each reason about the mesh's structure rather than about a
# convenience: "this is the realm's control surface" is a reason, "it does not seal
# yet" is not. A service that does not seal belongs in services.tsv and in an opt-out,
# never here.
# Both entries below come from the first real listing (2026-10-31), which carried 17
# ring procedures and 9 realm procedures beside the services.

column2: agent-to-agent contact: an inviter's own namespace, served to one peer, carrying an unguessable room. It is not a capability a service offers and it is not relayed traffic.
